The Prophet hid behind date-palms to overhear Ibn Saiyad, but his mother alerted him, and the Prophet said he would otherwise have revealed his reality.
A woman finally divorced by Rifa'a and remarried was told she cannot return to him without full relations with her present husband.
When a woman said she had suckled Uqba and his wife, the Prophet asked how he could keep her, so he divorced her.
Umar says that since revelation has ended people are judged by their public deeds, their secrets left to Allah.
Paradise or Hell is affirmed for the dead whom people praise or blame, for believers are Allah's witnesses on earth, and even two attesting a Muslim's good character suffice.
Foster relations count like blood relations: Aisha's foster uncle may visit her, Hamza's daughter is unlawful to the Prophet, and fostership is valid only in the suckling period.
A woman's hand was cut off for theft at the Conquest, after which she repented and married, and an unmarried adulterer was ordered a hundred lashes and a year's exile.
The Prophet refused to witness an unequal gift to one son as injustice, and foretold people after the best generations who give witness unasked and break their vows.
The great sins are associating others with Allah, undutifulness to parents, murder and false witness, against which the Prophet warned repeatedly.
Hearing a man recite in the mosque, the Prophet asked mercy for him for recalling verses he had dropped, and asked mercy for Abbad on recognising his voice.
Bilal's adhan comes while it is still night, so eat and drink until the blind Ibn Um Maktum's adhan at dawn.
Knowing Makhrama's voice at the door, the Prophet came out with a garment he had kept for him, praising its qualities.
Asked whether a woman's witness is not half a man's, the women agreed, and the Prophet said this is because of the deficiency of a woman's mind.
When a black slave-woman said she had suckled Uqba and his wife, the Prophet told him to leave her.
Aisha tells how, left behind seeking her necklace, she was falsely accused, fell ill for a month, and was declared innocent by revelation, after which Abu Bakr resumed helping Mistah.
The Prophet said exaggerated praise cuts a man's neck or back; one should only say 'I think him so', vouching for no one before Allah.
Ibn Umar, refused for Uhud at fourteen, was allowed into the Trench battle at fifteen, the age a caliph called the limit of manhood; Friday bathing binds those reaching puberty.
In a dispute without evidence the defendant swears, and whoever swears falsely to seize a Muslim's property meets Allah angry, as verse 3:77, revealed about Al-Ash'ath, confirms.
When Hilal bin Umaiya accused his wife of adultery, the Prophet told him to bring proof or be lashed, then mentioned the li'an as in the Book.
Allah will not speak to one withholding surplus water, pledging to a ruler for gain or lying on oath in a sale, and false oaths for property anger Him.
A man asking about Islam is told of the five daily prayers, Ramadan's fast and zakat, more being voluntary, and will succeed if true to his word.
Whoever has to take an oath should swear by Allah or remain silent.
The Prophet may rule for the more persuasive party, but whatever is wrongly given that way is a piece of fire not to be taken.
Heraclius called keeping promises and trusts a prophet's quality, a hypocrite breaks promises, Abu Bakr paid what the Prophet promised Jabir, and Moses completed the longer term.
Ibn Abbas asks why Muslims question the people of the Scriptures, who changed their books, when they recite the Quran, Allah's latest and undistorted revelation.
Those keeping Allah's limits and those violating them are like people in a boat: stopping one who holes its bottom saves everyone, while leaving him destroys all.
When Um Al-Ala testified that Allah had blessed the dead Uthman bin Mazun, the Prophet said even he did not know what would be done to him.
The Prophet drew lots among his wives for journeys and gave each a day and night, and Sauda gave hers to Aisha.
If people knew the reward of the call to prayer and the first row they would cast lots for them, and they would crawl to the Fajr and Isha prayers.
While the Prophet made peace among Bani Amr bin Auf, Abu Bakr led the prayer and stepped back when he came; men should say Subhan Allah, clapping being for women.
The Prophet went to reconcile quarrelling people, a verse orders peace between fighting believers, a peacemaker saying good things is no liar, and spouses may reconcile on terms.
A bedouin ransomed his son, who committed adultery with his employer's wife, but the Prophet returned the ransom, ordered a hundred lashes and a year's exile, and had her stoned.
Whatever is innovated that is not in harmony with the principles of the religion is rejected.
At Hudaibiya the Prophet rubbed out 'Allah's Messenger' from the treaty, agreed to return pagans who came to him, and came the next year for three days with sheathed weapons.
Abdullah bin Sahl and Muhaiyisa went to Khaibar while it had a peace treaty with the Muslims.
When Ar-Rabi' broke a girl's tooth the Prophet ordered retaliation as Allah's law, but the girl's family forgave and accepted compensation, as Anas bin An-Nadr had sworn.
Al-Hasan bin Ali made peace with Muawiya on guaranteed terms, as the Prophet had said Allah may make peace between two great Muslim groups through this son of his.
The Prophet settled loud debt disputes: one who swore not to ease his debtor gave way, and Ka'b remitted half of what Ibn Abu Hadrad owed him.
Charity is due for every joint of the body, and each day establishing justice among people earns the reward of charity.
When an Ansari objected that Az-Zubair was the Prophet's cousin in their irrigation dispute, the Prophet gave Zubair his full right, and Zubair links a verse on accepting his judgement.
